title: Four Traps That Block UX Leaders
intro: From his UXPA 2026 keynote: Muriel Wilkins's seven hidden blockers, grouped into four traps for UX people at any level.

topics.title: Four Traps That Block UX Leaders

learn.title: The seven blockers
learn.text:
“I need to be involved.” · “I can't say no.” · “I need it done now.” · “I can't make a mistake.” · “I know I'm right.” · “If I can do it, so can you.” · “I don't belong here.”

Each starts as a strength that turned into a reflex.

try.q: What do the blockers have in common?
options: Each is a strength that became a reflex
Each is a response to a difficult manager
try.explain: The value isn't the problem; the automatic reaction is.

learn.title: Four traps
learn.text:
**Over-functioning** — “I need to be involved” and “I can't say no”
→ reframe: where do I add the *most* value? When does saying yes truly matter?

**Pacing and perfection** — “I need it done now” and “I can't make a mistake”
→ panic or paralysis, both expensive

**Partnership** — “I know I'm right” and “If I can do it, so can you”

**Leader identity** — “I don't belong here”: waiting for permission to lead

try.q: Which trap pairs “I need it done now” with “I can't make a mistake”?
try.explain: Panic and paralysis are two faces of the same trap.

right.label: The reframe
items: Where do I add most value?
What pace does this actually need?

learn.title: Why UX people get these
learn.text:
Wanting to be involved often comes from **knowing UX gets brought in too late**. That experience is real — the reflex it creates isn't always useful.

The self-coaching loop: notice the trigger (an invitation, a deadline, a challenge), name the blocker, ask what it's protecting, choose the reframe, act — then review afterwards.

try.q: What is the first step of the self-coaching loop?
try.explain: An invitation, a deadline or a challenge.

test.q: Whose book is this based on?
How many hidden blockers does Wilkins describe?
test.explain: Calabro groups them into four traps.

test.q: Which blocker belongs to the leader-identity trap?
Why do UX people often feel they must be involved in everything?
options: They know UX gets brought in too late
Their teams are almost always understaffed
test.explain: A real experience, turned into an automatic reaction.

test.q: What does the loop end with?
test.explain: Notice, name, ask, reframe, act, review.
